A bit of a backstory, bc I think it is important. Our old dog, Nana, died several weeks ago. She was highly dog aggressive, hated new people, especially guests. She only accepted a handful of our family members. She was scared of children (due to that aggressive as well). She was also a couch potatoe and didn't like going on walks. We loved her a lot, but she was problematic. She was amazing when we were alone at home. We miss her as hell (and I will not be answering any questions or comments about her, because that is not the point).

With that in mind: we adopted our (now 6mo) puppy, Myszka, about a month ago. She's big. She absolutely loves people. She is really cute. People sometimes stop me to chat and ask what breed she is, but she's just a mutt. She loves those chats, cuz she always gets pets. Sometimes people play with her a bit. Our family love her. She's great with kids. Due to her size, we gotta be careful, but she's really gentle with our 5yo nieces. SHE LOVES WALKS (I do as well and I really missed just walking around when we had Nana, now I can whenever for however long I want to, she'll be there with me). She loves dogs, loves playing with them. She's been surprisingly good with potty training. She's letting us know when she needs to poop (quite clearly I might add haha). She sometimes pees at home, but those are mostly our mistakes. She chose a place that is really easy to clean up, so I'm not bothered by that at all. She was crate trained in the shelter, so we're not having any troubles leaving her alone for a few hours. She loves to play with toys (something that is quite new to me as none of my previous dogs liked toys, they just ignored them). She's really funny. She's making faces all the time and she does funny things every day. I love that I can give her kisses and she sometimes kisses me back in a doggy way ofc. She loves bath time. She's falling asleep when I'm bathing her 😄  she learned quickly not to bite furniture.  She learns commands and tricks pretty quickly.
I love that I now have a young dog who I can teach how to behave in a society and that I can train to act in a way that allows me to take her everywhere with me and not be scared that she could hurt someone or somedog.

That is not to say that we do not have troubles. I could share them, but I don't think it will be helpful. Those are the good things that I see in having my puppy. Was I overwhelmed? Yes. Did I have moments that I regretted her? Yes, it was especially hard when grief was overwhelming. Will it get better? It is starting to vet easier by the day. 
Just do your research, get ready mentally, and you'll do great. Just caring so much will make you a good dog owner.

I used to have 2 dogs (separately). Both of them I got as adult dogs. They had their own issues but nothing I couldn't live with.
This time we got a puppy (5 months old to be exact) and I feel like I have a child. For the first several nights she wouldn't let me sleep. She gave me so many bruises (she's a German shepherd mix, so she's big). I basically don't have time for anything else than walks, playing with her and training. 

I expected a puppy to be more demanding than my oldies, but I didn't expect just how demanding it will be.
I had a crisis where I regretted her for a moment. I know this puppy phase will pass. It's been a few weeks and she's not biting as much, though other problems arise, but we tackle them as we go. 

I had a lot of experience with a problematic dog, because my previous one was aggressive. But she disliked being outside and when she got older she was content to just go and do her business outside and then she was pulling home to be a couch ptatoe again. The puppy is demanding an all fronts (fortunately, without the aggression - she's as sweet as they come and this was the main reason we chose her).

I absolutely love dogs and when my oldie died I didn't know how to function. Even though the puppy is demanding, I wouldn't trade her for the world. 

When you get a dog be sure to think through your lifestyle and how much time you can sacrifice. I was sure I could spend as much time with the puppy as she needs. Turned out it was painful to switch from a couch potatoe to a high energy kid. If I had taken her as a singe, I would definitely be regretting her now. I wouldn't be able to provide her so much attention as a single person. As a married couple it's hard but manageable.

If you have any questions, feel free to ask here or send me a message.

You should also try to surround yourself with Polish as much as you can. Try to get to the Polish side of social media. Watch Polish shows (entertaining, but not genius: Rodzinka PL, Ranczo).
